sourceText: - **829. Dose finding** \[Slider\]: place doses where they best pin down a dose-response curve.
title: A dose score changes response chance
lens: the response probability before calculating design information

sourceText: - **830. Adaptive design** \[Slider\]: each new measurement is chosen where the model is least sure.
title: Uncertainty affects an acquisition score
lens: the uncertainty bonus in one adaptive measurement choice

sourceText: - **831. Paired designs** \[Split\]: test each person under both conditions and noise drops sharply.
title: Pairing removes shared variation
lens: the covariance term in a paired mean-difference standard error

sourceText: - **832. Factorial design** \[Slider\]: test 3 factors in 8 runs and read off every main effect and interaction.
title: An interaction contributes to a response
lens: the stipulated product contribution in a factorial illustration

sourceText: - **833. Fractional factorial** \[Slider\]: halve the runs, at the cost of confusing some interactions.
title: Aliased effects share a contrast
lens: the unresolved mixture of two effects in a reduced design

sourceText: - **834. Latin square** \[Slider\]: balance two nuisance factors, like day and machine, in one grid.
title: A balanced grid has many assignments
lens: the combinatorial assignment count before Latin-square restrictions

sourceText: - **835. Response surface** \[Slider\]: climb toward the best settings of two factors with small designed experiments.
title: A local response slope guides a move
lens: one local directional slope before response-surface optimization

sourceText: - **836. Power by simulation** \[Slider\]: simulate your exact design thousands of times to estimate power.
title: Count significant simulated replicates
lens: an illustrative rejection-count distribution under fixed power

sourceText: - **837. Shared control arm** \[Slider\]: test four treatments against one control and save sample size.
title: A shared control affects precision
lens: the control sample size in one independent mean contrast

sourceText: - **838. Ethics of adaptive allocation** \[Split\]: more patients get the better arm, but inference gets harder.
title: Adaptive trial allocation changes yield
lens: the reward mix before adaptive-inference corrections

sourceText: - **839. Stop at enough precision** \[Slider\]: end data collection once the interval is narrow enough.
title: A tighter target needs more samples
lens: the normal-approximation precision target before sequential stopping

sourceText: - **840. Is the test worth running?** \[Slider\]: compare the expected value of information with the cost of testing.
title: A test's expected benefit meets cost
lens: a supplied value-of-information benefit and testing cost

sourceText: - **841. Star-rating spillover** \[Slider\]: a new rating algorithm boosts treated products' displayed stars; buyers shift from control products, so the A/B lift is mostly stolen sales. Slide the substitution rate and watch the bias grow.
title: A rating lift can steal control sales
lens: the control displacement inflating a measured sales contrast

sourceText: - **842. Sellers react to both arms** \[Gotcha\]: when a rating formula changes, sellers adjust behavior for all buyers, contaminating control.
title: Sellers change outcomes across arms
lens: the cross-arm behavioral spillover in a stipulated seller model

sourceText: - **843. Randomize users or items?** \[Split\]: the same rating change tested by user split and by item split gives opposite biases.
title: The split changes stolen sales
lens: the substitution exposure under two assumed split designs

sourceText: - **844. Two-sided randomization** \[Slider\]: randomize both buyers and listings to bound the bias from each side (Johari et al., 2022).
title: Both sides determine exposure
lens: a two-sided exposure count before a randomization estimator

sourceText: - **845. Graph cluster randomization** \[Slider\]: treat whole friend clusters so most people's friends share their arm.
title: Cluster peers share treatment
lens: the number of treated neighbors within an illustrative cluster

sourceText: - **846. Exposure mapping** \[Slider\]: color each user by the share of treated friends and estimate effects by exposure level.
title: Exposure depends on treated neighbors
lens: the exposure map in a declared linear spillover model

sourceText: - **847. Shared ad budgets** \[Gotcha\]: treated campaigns spend budget faster, starving control campaigns that share it.
title: A shared budget can starve controls
lens: the shared resource remaining after faster treatment spending

sourceText: - **848. Geo experiments** \[Slider\]: randomize whole cities to measure a marketing change without spillover between users.
title: Geographic separation reduces leakage
lens: the cross-boundary exposure assumed in a geo design

sourceText: - **850. Ratings feedback loop** \[Slider\]: higher displayed stars bring more sales, more reviews and even higher stars.
title: Stars and sales can amplify each other
lens: the stipulated feedback multiplier of a rating loop

sourceText: - **851. Inflated ratings** \[Story\]: most Airbnb listings rate 4.5 stars or higher, compressing ratings' signal (Zervas, Proserpio & Byers, 2021).
title: Compressed stars carry a smaller gap
lens: the response scale of an illustrative ratings display

sourceText: - **852. Herding on votes** \[Story\]: one random early upvote raised a comment's final rating about 25% on a news site (Muchnik, Aral & Taylor, 2013).
title: An early vote gets amplified
lens: the initial vote in a toy herding recurrence

sourceText: - **853. Influence or similarity?** \[Split\]: friends behave alike because they influence each other or because they chose similar friends.
title: Similarity need not mean peer influence
lens: the shared-cause path in a friendship illustration

sourceText: - **854. The reflection problem** \[Gotcha\]: group averages can't separate peer influence from shared circumstances (Manski, 1993).
title: Peer association has a shared cause
lens: the observational ambiguity of a stipulated peer model

sourceText: - **855. Deworming spillovers** \[Story\]: treating children for worms also reduced infection in untreated nearby schools (Miguel & Kremer, 2004).
title: An untreated neighbor can benefit
lens: a positive neighborhood treatment externality in a toy model

sourceText: - **856. Global vs A/B effect** \[Slider\]: the effect of launching to everyone differs from what a 50/50 test measures.
title: A full rollout changes peer exposure
lens: the treatment saturation behind a policy effect

sourceText: - **857. Shared inventory** \[Slider\]: a pricing test sells out stock that control customers also needed.
title: A test draws on shared inventory
lens: the depletion rate of a common stock buffer

sourceText: - **859. Shared training data** \[Gotcha\]: both arms of a recommender test feed one model, so treatment leaks into control.
title: Shared training mixes treatment data
lens: the data composition entering a shared model update

sourceText: - **860. Cluster size trade-off** \[Slider\]: bigger clusters cut spillover bias but leave fewer units, so variance rises.
title: Larger clusters leave fewer units
lens: the independent-cluster count before cluster-size design effects

sourceText: - **861. Front-door** \[Slider\]: with an unmeasured confounder between smoking and cancer, go through tar deposits to recover the effect.
title: A mediator carries a declared path
lens: the mediated coefficient under stated no-confounding assumptions

sourceText: - **862. No-assumption bounds** \[Slider\]: with nothing assumed, the effect lies in an interval; watch its width (Manski, 1990).
title: Unknown counterfactuals leave bounds
lens: the treatment share in binary worst-case effect bounds

sourceText: - **863. Add an assumption** \[Slider\]: assume monotone effects and the bounds snap tighter.
title: A no-harm assumption tightens a bound
lens: the monotone-response restriction on a partial identification set

sourceText: - **865. Transport a trial** \[Slider\]: reweight a trial's patients to match a different target population.
title: A new population changes average effect
lens: the target population mix under transportable group effects

sourceText: - **866. Selection diagrams** \[Slider\]: mark where two populations differ in a graph and see whether results can transfer.
title: Transport needs a target composition
lens: the population shift under an explicit effect-invariance assumption

sourceText: - **867. Proximal inference** \[Slider\]: two imperfect proxies of a hidden confounder can together recover an effect.
title: A proxy method needs identification
lens: the confounding gap before a proximal bridge is identified

sourceText: - **868. Negative control exposure** \[Slider\]: an exposure that can't cause the outcome but shares its confounders reveals bias.
title: A negative control can reveal bias
lens: the noncausal association of a declared null exposure

sourceText: - **870. Truncation by death** \[Gotcha\]: comparing quality of life among survivors compares different kinds of people across arms.
title: Survivors can be different people
lens: outcome-dependent survival in a selected mean

sourceText: - **871. Bunching at a kink** \[Slider\]: incomes pile up just below a tax threshold; the pile's size reveals how people respond to taxes.
title: A threshold can change local outcomes
lens: a descriptive threshold jump before structural bunching inference

sourceText: - **872. Shift-share instruments** \[Slider\]: national industry shocks weighted by local industry mix create regional variation.
title: Industry weights transmit shocks
lens: the local exposure-weighted shift rather than instrument validity

sourceText: - **873. Random judges** \[Story\]: cases randomly assigned to stricter or more lenient judges reveal effects of incarceration.
title: Judge assignment supplies a first stage
lens: the assumed valid-instrument ratio in a judge illustration

sourceText: - **874. Mendelian randomization** \[Story\]: genes randomly inherited at conception act as instruments for exposures like alcohol use.
title: A genetic instrument needs assumptions
lens: the first-stage denominator under stipulated IV validity

sourceText: - **875. Sensitivity contours** \[Slider\]: plot how strong a confounder must be, against treatment and outcome, to erase the estimate (Cinelli & Hazlett, 2020).
title: Bias depends on two common-cause links
lens: the omitted-variable contribution to an observational slope

sourceText: - **876. Placebo synthetic controls** \[Slider\]: rerun synthetic control on every untreated region and see if the real effect stands out.
title: A placebo gap needs a benchmark
lens: the observed-minus-synthetic gap before a placebo ranking

sourceText: - **877. Changes-in-changes** \[Slider\]: compare whole distributions before and after, not just means.
title: A distribution has unequal group shifts
lens: the quantile-group composition in a distributional contrast

sourceText: - **878. Overlap weights** \[Slider\]: weight people in the region where treated and control truly overlap, avoiding extreme weights.
title: Balance the region of common support
lens: the balancing weight before overlap-weighted causal estimation

sourceText: - **879. Trial plus real-world data** \[Slider\]: combine a small trial with a big observational dataset, letting the trial correct the bias.
title: Combine a trial and a corrected estimate
lens: the stipulated estimator weights after observational bias correction

sourceText: - **880. Mismeasured treatment** \[Gotcha\]: if "treated" is recorded with errors, the estimated effect shrinks toward zero.
title: Measurement error attenuates a slope
lens: the assumed reliability factor multiplying an effect

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **881. Group-time effects** \[Slider\]: a grid of effects for each adoption cohort and each period, then aggregated (Callaway & Sant'Anna, 2021).
title: Aggregate group-time effects explicitly
lens: the cohort weights behind a declared causal aggregation

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **882. Clean event study** \[Slider\]: compare naive and interaction-weighted event-study plots under staggered adoption (Sun & Abraham, 2021).
title: Event-study weights change the target
lens: the supplied positive or negative cohort weights

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **883. Forbidden comparisons** \[Slider\]: a bar chart of the hidden 2×2 comparisons inside two-way fixed effects, including bad ones using already-treated units as controls.
title: A forbidden comparison can get weight
lens: the negative component in a toy fixed-effect decomposition

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **885. Synthetic diff-in-diff** \[Slider\]: weight both units and time periods to blend synthetic control with diff-in-diff (Arkhangelsky et al., 2021).
title: A weighted control also has a trend
lens: the control trend after unit and time weighting

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **886. Weak pre-trend tests** \[Gotcha\]: passing a pre-trend test often says little, because the test has low power (Roth, 2022).
title: A noisy pretrend may look insignificant
lens: the standard error behind a pretrend diagnostic

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **888. Treatment dose** \[Slider\]: diff-in-diff when regions get different intensities of a policy.
title: Policy intensity changes a contrast
lens: the stipulated dose slope under a parallel-trend assumption

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **889. CausalImpact** \[Slider\]: a Bayesian structural time series predicts the no-campaign path; the gap is the effect (Brodersen et al., 2015).
title: A campaign gap needs a counterfactual
lens: the supplied no-campaign prediction rather than fitted causal proof

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **890. Seasonal interruption** \[Slider\]: model weekly and yearly cycles before estimating a policy's break.
title: Seasonality belongs in the baseline
lens: the common seasonal change removed by a control contrast
